accepted.s:
The Insecticides Act, 1968 and the Insecticides Rules, 1971 provide for the establishment of which of the following bodies?
1. Central Insecticides Board
2. Registration Committee
3. National Pesticides Tribunal
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Insecticides Act, 1968 and Rules, 1971 set up the Central Insecticides Board and the Registration Committee. A National Pesticides Tribunal is not mentioned as a body created by these provisions.
accepted.tq: Identify the correctly stated statutory bodies and reject the invented institutional name.
accepted.sec: Pesticides - Insecticides Act, bans, neem pesticides, IPM  [other exams]

accepted.s: The Draft Pesticides Management Bill, 2025 is intended to replace which of the following?
o: The Fertilisers Act, 1952 and Fertiliser Control Order, 1985
The Seeds Act, 1966 and Seeds Rules, 1968
The Insecticides Act, 1968 and Insecticides Rules, 1971
The Essential Commodities Act, 1955 and its agricultural orders
accepted.x: The Draft Pesticides Management Bill, 2025 proposes to replace the Insecticides Act, 1968 and the Insecticides Rules, 1971.
accepted.tq: Use the replace-the-existing-law pattern and distinguish neighbouring agricultural laws.
accepted.sec: Pesticides - Insecticides Act, bans, neem pesticides, IPM  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is a stated feature of the Draft Pesticides Management Bill, 2025?
o: Reduction of penalties for pesticide violations
Transfer of pesticide registration exclusively to State governments
Higher penalties and promotion of biological pesticides
accepted.x: The draft Bill proposes higher penalties and promotes biological pesticides.
accepted.tq: Match the policy proposal with its specific reform objectives.
accepted.sec: Pesticides - Insecticides Act, bans, neem pesticides, IPM  [other exams]

accepted.s: The deadline for submitting comments on the Draft Pesticides Management Bill, 2025 was:
accepted.x: Comments on the Draft Pesticides Management Bill, 2025 were due by 4 February 2026.
accepted.tq: Separate the consultation deadline from the date of the report carrying the information.
accepted.sec: Pesticides - Insecticides Act, bans, neem pesticides, IPM  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. India continues to use at least 66 pesticides that are banned elsewhere.
2. Aldrin was associated with the killing of mugger crocodiles in Kota.
3. Endosulfan was banned by the Supreme Court in 2011.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct: at least 66 pesticides used in India are banned elsewhere, Aldrin killed mugger crocodiles in Kota, and the Supreme Court banned Endosulfan in 2011.
accepted.tq: Combine three related pesticide facts and select the complete set of correct statements.
accepted.sec: Pesticides - Insecticides Act, bans, neem pesticides, IPM  [other exams]

accepted.s: Neem-based pesticides are classified as:
accepted.x: Neem-based pesticides are bio-pesticides.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between biological and chemical pesticide categories.
accepted.sec: Pesticides - Insecticides Act, bans, neem pesticides, IPM  [other exams]

accepted.s: Integrated Pest Management primarily combines:
o: Biological, cultural and need-based chemical control
accepted.x: IPM combines biological control, cultural control and need-based chemical control in order to reduce pesticide use.
accepted.tq: Identify the management approach from the combination of control methods rather than from one component alone.
accepted.sec: Pesticides - Insecticides Act, bans, neem pesticides, IPM  [other exams]

accepted.s: The Soil Health Card scheme was launched on 19 February 2015 at:
accepted.x: The Soil Health Card scheme was launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on 19 February 2015 at Suratgarh in Rajasthan.
accepted.tq: Combine the date and location to distinguish the launch event from similar agricultural initiatives.
accepted.sec: Soil Health Card scheme - objectives, parameters, cycle  [other exams]

accepted.s: Since 2022-23, the Soil Health Card scheme has been part of Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana under the name:
accepted.x: Since 2022-23, the scheme has been included in RKVY as “Soil Health and Fertility”.
accepted.tq: Apply the ministry-scheme sub-component distinction and identify the exact official title.
accepted.sec: Soil Health Card scheme - objectives, parameters, cycle  [other exams]

accepted.s: Soil Health Cards are issued once in every:
accepted.x: Soil Health Cards are issued every two years and provide crop-wise nutrient dosages.
accepted.tq: Test the scheme cycle through closely spaced numerical alternatives.
accepted.sec: Soil Health Card scheme - objectives, parameters, cycle  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following sets contains only parameters tested under the Soil Health Card scheme?
o: Nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, sulphur and pH
Calcium, magnesium, sodium, chlorine and salinity only
Nitrogen, rainfall, temperature, humidity and pH
Phosphorus, potassium, crop yield, irrigation and rainfall
accepted.x: The Soil Health Card tests nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, sulphur, zinc, iron, copper, manganese, boron, pH, electrical conductivity and organic carbon. The other alternatives include non-Soil Health Card parameters or omit the specified nutrient set.
accepted.tq: Separate soil-nutrient parameters from climatic, crop and irrigation indicators.
accepted.sec: Soil Health Card scheme - objectives, parameters, cycle  [other exams]

accepted.s: How many parameters are tested under the Soil Health Card scheme?
accepted.x: The scheme tests 12 parameters: N, P, K, S, Zn, Fe, Cu, Mn, B, pH, EC and organic carbon.
accepted.tq: Use the exact quantitative value after identifying the complete parameter list.
accepted.sec: Soil Health Card scheme - objectives, parameters, cycle  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly represents the Soil Health Card figures stated for Andhra Pradesh in 2025-26?
o: 25.55 crore samples collected and 6 lakh tested
6 lakh samples collected and 5.52 lakh tested
6 lakh cards issued and 5.52 crore samples tested
5.52 lakh samples collected and 6 lakh tested
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh collected 6 lakh soil samples and tested 5.52 lakh samples in 2025-26.
accepted.tq: Keep collection and testing figures in their correct order and units.
accepted.sec: Soil Health Card scheme - objectives, parameters, cycle  [other exams]

accepted.s: The number of Soil Health Cards issued nationally is reported to be over:
accepted.x: More than 25.55 crore Soil Health Cards have been issued nationally.
accepted.tq: Distinguish crore-scale quantities by place value and decimal position.
accepted.sec: Soil Health Card scheme - objectives, parameters, cycle  [other exams]

accepted.s:
With reference to agricultural technology projects, consider the following statements:
1. NATP was launched in 1998.
2. NATP was World Bank-aided.
3. NAIP was implemented during 2006-2014.
4. NAIP was World Bank-funded.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: NATP began in 1998 with World Bank aid, while NAIP ran from 2006 to 2014 and was also World Bank-funded.
accepted.tq: Check each project against its year, duration and funding source before selecting the coded combination.
accepted.sec: ICAR technology projects - NATP, NAIP  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which of the following was NOT a component of the National Agricultural Innovation Project?
o: ICAR as a catalyst for change
accepted.x: NAIP components included ICAR as a catalyst for change, production-to-consumption research, sustainable rural livelihood security, and basic and strategic research. Universal crop-price stabilisation was not listed as a component.
accepted.tq: Find the option that does not belong to the stated project-component group.
accepted.sec: ICAR technology projects - NATP, NAIP  [other exams]

accepted.s: The Sub-Mission on Agricultural Mechanisation (SMAM) covered the period from:
accepted.x: The period stated for SMAM is 2014-15 to 2025-26.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the exact start and end years from nearby scheme periods.
accepted.sec: Farm mechanisation - SMAM, custom hiring, Drone Didi

accepted.s: During 2014-15 to 2025-26, SMAM subsidised approximately how many machines?
accepted.x: SMAM subsidised 20.93 lakh machines during 2014-15 to 2025-26.
accepted.tq: Read the lakh–crore scale carefully when interpreting a large programme figure.
accepted.sec: Farm mechanisation - SMAM, custom hiring, Drone Didi

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly states the SMAM custom hiring centre figures?
o: 25,689 nationally and 2,395 in Andhra Pradesh in 2025-26
27,563 nationally and 239 in Andhra Pradesh in 2025-26
accepted.x: The stated SMAM figures are 27,563 custom hiring centres nationally and 239 in Andhra Pradesh in 2025-26. A separate Economic Survey count gives 25,689 national CHCs.
accepted.tq: Compare national and State figures without interchanging the geographical level.
accepted.sec: Farm mechanisation - SMAM, custom hiring, Drone Didi

accepted.s: Namo Drone Didi provides drones primarily to:
accepted.x: Namo Drone Didi provides drones to women’s Self-Help Groups.
accepted.tq: Identify the intended beneficiary group rather than the implementing or regulating institution.
accepted.sec: Farm mechanisation - SMAM, custom hiring, Drone Didi

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly compares the reported distribution of Namo Drone Didi drones?
accepted.x: Five hundred drones had been distributed nationally, while Andhra Pradesh had given 529 drones according to the cited State figures.
accepted.tq: Separate national and State totals instead of assuming that the State figure must be lower.
accepted.sec: Farm mechanisation - SMAM, custom hiring, Drone Didi

accepted.s: The Standard Operating Procedure for drone spraying was issued on:
accepted.x: The SOP for drone spraying, including crop-specific SOPs, was issued on 20 April 2023.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the operational guideline date from scheme-launch and current-report dates.
accepted.sec: Farm mechanisation - SMAM, custom hiring, Drone Didi

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly states Andhra Pradesh’s SMAM position for 2025-26?
accepted.x: In 2025-26, Andhra Pradesh reported 38,610 machines, 239 custom hiring centres and expenditure of ₹169.32 crore under SMAM.
accepted.tq: Match a State-year data bundle without substituting figures from another year or programme.
accepted.sec: Farm mechanisation - SMAM, custom hiring, Drone Didi

accepted.s: India’s farm mechanisation level is estimated at approximately:
accepted.x: India’s farm mechanisation level is reported as 40-45 percent.
accepted.tq: Select the precise range rather than a rounded but unsupported estimate.
accepted.sec: Farm mechanisation - SMAM, custom hiring, Drone Didi

accepted.s:
Which of the following correctly represents the major SMAM figures for 2014-15 to 2025-26?
1. ₹9,639.96 crore allocated for mechanisation
2. 20.93 lakh machines subsidised
3. 646 hi-tech hubs
4. 25,260 farm machinery banks
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four figures are stated for the period 2014-15 to 2025-26: ₹9,639.96 crore, 20.93 lakh machines, 646 hi-tech hubs and 25,260 farm machinery banks.
accepted.tq: Verify a multi-figure programme profile rather than relying on one familiar statistic.

accepted.s: Under SMAM, the amount stated for Kisan drones is:
accepted.x: ₹141.41 crore was provided for Kisan drones under SMAM.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the drone-specific allocation from total or State-level mechanisation expenditure.
accepted.sec: Farm mechanisation - SMAM, custom hiring, Drone Didi

accepted.s: Under Andhra Pradesh SMAM in 2024-25, the expenditure and number of farmers covered were respectively:
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh spent ₹75.80 crore and covered 42,864 farmers under SMAM in 2024-25.
accepted.tq: Pair the correct year with the corresponding expenditure and beneficiary count.

accepted.s: Which of the following is the scientific core of the Green Revolution package?
accepted.x: Although the package included HYV seeds, chemical fertilisers, assured irrigation, pesticides and mechanisation, the scientific core was the use of HYV seeds.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the central technological element from the other complementary inputs.
accepted.sec: Green Revolution technology and persons - HYV origin, key figures, phases, Second and Evergreen Revolution  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The HYV wheat varieties associated with Norman Borlaug’s Mexican dwarf wheats include:
accepted.x: Kalyan Sona and Sonalika were associated with HYV wheat derived from Norman Borlaug’s Mexican dwarf wheats.
accepted.tq: Link the person, crop and specific varieties in a name-based agricultural question.
accepted.sec: Green Revolution technology and persons - HYV origin, key figures, phases, Second and Evergreen Revolution  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: IR-8 rice was developed at:
accepted.x: IR-8 rice originated from the International Rice Research Institute (IRRI) in the Philippines.
accepted.tq: Use institution–country association to distinguish rice research from wheat research.
accepted.sec: Green Revolution technology and persons - HYV origin, key figures, phases, Second and Evergreen Revolution  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: M.S. Swaminathan is widely associated with being the:
accepted.x: M.S. Swaminathan is identified as the father of India’s Green Revolution.
accepted.tq: Match the prominent personality with the specific agricultural transformation.
accepted.sec: Green Revolution technology and persons - HYV origin, key figures, phases, Second and Evergreen Revolution  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which sequence correctly describes the adoption and expansion of hybrid and HYV seeds in India?
o: Hybrid seeds from 1960; widespread adoption by 1963; full-fledged HYV programme from 1966
Hybrid seeds from 1966; widespread adoption by 1971; full-fledged programme from 1980
Hybrid seeds from 1951; widespread adoption by 1955; full-fledged programme from 1960
Hybrid seeds from 1963; widespread adoption by 1966; full-fledged programme from 1968
accepted.x: Hybrid seeds appeared from 1960, were widely adopted by 1963, and the HYV programme became full-fledged from 1966.
accepted.tq: Arrange closely spaced agricultural milestones in their correct sequence.
accepted.sec: Green Revolution technology and persons - HYV origin, key figures, phases, Second and Evergreen Revolution  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The HYV programme became full-fledged from 1966 following which combination of circumstances?
o: Introduction of the WTO and the launch of PMKSY
Two successive drought years, decline in foodgrain output and dependence on PL-480
A sharp rise in foodgrain output and complete food self-sufficiency
Abolition of irrigation projects and withdrawal of fertiliser subsidies
accepted.x: The programme became full-fledged from 1966 after the 1965-66 and 1966-67 droughts, foodgrain production fell to 72.3 and 74.2 MT, and India depended on PL-480 supplies.
accepted.tq: Connect the policy response with the crisis conditions that necessitated it.
accepted.sec: Green Revolution technology and persons - HYV origin, key figures, phases, Second and Evergreen Revolution  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The foodgrain production figures associated with the drought years 1965-66 and 1966-67 were respectively:
accepted.x: Foodgrain production fell to 72.3 million tonnes in 1965-66 and 74.2 million tonnes in 1966-67.
accepted.tq: Test the order of year-wise figures rather than only recognising the two numbers.
accepted.sec: Green Revolution technology and persons - HYV origin, key figures, phases, Second and Evergreen Revolution  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Which one of the following correctly matches the phases of the Green Revolution with their periods?
A. Pre-Green Revolution
B. Early Green Revolution
C. Later Green Revolution

1. 1951-68
2. 1968-81
3. 1987-92
accepted.x: The Pre-Green Revolution phase was 1951-68, the Early Green Revolution was 1968-81, and the Later Green Revolution was 1987-92.
accepted.tq: Start with the phase-year pair that is most certain and eliminate inconsistent codes.
accepted.sec: Green Revolution technology and persons - HYV origin, key figures, phases, Second and Evergreen Revolution  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following in chronological order:
A. Intensive Agriculture District Programme
B. First Green Revolution period ended
C. Establishment of M.S. Swaminathan Research Foundation
accepted.x: The order is IADP in 1960-61, the end of the first Green Revolution period, and establishment of the M.S. Swaminathan Research Foundation in 1988.
accepted.tq: Use the dated anchor at the beginning and the 1988 institution as the final anchor.
accepted.sec: Green Revolution technology and persons - HYV origin, key figures, phases, Second and Evergreen Revolution  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The call for a Second Green Revolution in India was made by:
accepted.x: Prime Minister Manmohan Singh called for a Second Green Revolution.
accepted.tq: Match the policy call with the person associated with it, avoiding confusion with agricultural scientists.
accepted.sec: Green Revolution technology and persons - HYV origin, key figures, phases, Second and Evergreen Revolution  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
The focus of the proposed Second Green Revolution included which of the following?
1. Pulses and oilseeds
2. Millets
3. Precision farming and micro-irrigation
4. Exclusive expansion of chemical pesticide use
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Second Green Revolution focus included pulses, oilseeds, millets, precision farming and micro-irrigation. Exclusive expansion of chemical pesticide use was not part of the stated focus.
accepted.tq: Reject an extreme exclusive claim while retaining the listed diversification and efficiency measures.
accepted.sec: Green Revolution technology and persons - HYV origin, key figures, phases, Second and Evergreen Revolution  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The concept of the Evergreen Revolution, associated with M.S. Swaminathan, refers to:
o: Replacement of all traditional crops by HYV crops
Permanent increase in productivity without ecological harm
Expansion of agriculture only through irrigation-intensive farming
Continuous use of chemical inputs irrespective of environmental effects
accepted.x: The Evergreen Revolution means productivity improvement in perpetuity without ecological harm.
accepted.tq: Identify the definition by combining productivity growth with ecological sustainability.
accepted.sec: Green Revolution technology and persons - HYV origin, key figures, phases, Second and Evergreen Revolution  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which PMKSY component is primarily concerned with the faster completion of major and medium irrigation projects?
accepted.x: The Accelerated Irrigation Benefits Programme (AIBP) is intended for faster completion of major and medium projects.
accepted.tq: Match the irrigation component with its precise functional objective.
accepted.sec: Irrigation inputs - micro-irrigation, PMKSY components, PM-KUSUM, tubewell area  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Har Khet Ko Pani under PMKSY includes which of the following?
1. Command Area Development and Water Management
2. Surface minor irrigation
3. Repair, renovation and restoration of water bodies
4. Groundwater development
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Har Khet Ko Pani includes CAD&WM, surface minor irrigation, repair, renovation and restoration of water bodies, and groundwater-related measures.
accepted.tq: Treat the component as a bundle of irrigation-delivery measures and test every listed element.
accepted.sec: Irrigation inputs - micro-irrigation, PMKSY components, PM-KUSUM, tubewell area  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Per Drop More Crop under PMKSY is primarily associated with:
accepted.x: Per Drop More Crop focuses on micro-irrigation. It was under PMKSY from 2015 to December 2021 and is now under RKVY.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the component’s functional focus from its administrative placement.
accepted.sec: Irrigation inputs - micro-irrigation, PMKSY components, PM-KUSUM, tubewell area  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the present administrative position of Per Drop More Crop?
o: It remained under PMKSY after December 2021 without change
It was under RKVY from 2015 to 2021 and is now under PMKSY
It was under PMKSY from 2015 to December 2021 and is now under RKVY
accepted.x: Per Drop More Crop was under PMKSY from 2015 to December 2021 and is now administered under RKVY.
accepted.tq: Track the scheme’s transfer between programmes by using the time boundary as the discriminator.
accepted.sec: Irrigation inputs - micro-irrigation, PMKSY components, PM-KUSUM, tubewell area  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Micro-irrigation, including drip and sprinkler systems, conserves water primarily by:
o: Delivering water more efficiently to the crop zone
Increasing evaporation from the soil surface
Replacing all groundwater with surface water
Eliminating the need for crop selection
accepted.x: Drip and sprinkler systems improve the efficiency of water application and thereby conserve water.
accepted.tq: Apply the underlying resource-efficiency principle to a farm-level situation.
accepted.sec: Irrigation inputs - micro-irrigation, PMKSY components, PM-KUSUM, tubewell area  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The PDMC programme has brought approximately how much area under micro-irrigation?
accepted.x: PDMC has brought 109 lakh hectares under micro-irrigation.
accepted.tq: Distinguish lakh and crore expressions for the same scale of land coverage.
accepted.sec: Irrigation inputs - micro-irrigation, PMKSY components, PM-KUSUM, tubewell area  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The subsidy under the micro-irrigation programme may be provided up to what proportion, subject to a cap of 5 hectares?
accepted.x: The subsidy may extend up to 55 percent, with a cap of 5 hectares.
accepted.tq: Combine the percentage ceiling with the area cap to identify the precise provision.
accepted.sec: Irrigation inputs - micro-irrigation, PMKSY components, PM-KUSUM, tubewell area  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: PM-KUSUM, launched in 2019, is associated with:
o: Construction of major irrigation dams only
Distribution of chemical fertilisers through cooperatives
Replacement of all farm pumps by diesel pumps
Solar pumps and solarisation of grid-connected agricultural pumps
accepted.x: PM-KUSUM promotes solar pumps and the solarisation of grid-connected farm pumps.
accepted.tq: Match the scheme with its energy technology and avoid confusing it with irrigation-construction programmes.
accepted.sec: Irrigation inputs - micro-irrigation, PMKSY components, PM-KUSUM, tubewell area  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The effect of solar irrigation on groundwater extraction depends particularly on:
o: The number of Soil Health Cards issued
The size of the fertiliser subsidy alone
Only the number of tractors in the district
accepted.x: Solar irrigation may lead to over-extraction of groundwater depending on hydrogeology and the crops being grown.
accepted.tq: Apply the conditional environmental effect instead of treating a technology as universally beneficial or harmful.
accepted.sec: Irrigation inputs - micro-irrigation, PMKSY components, PM-KUSUM, tubewell area  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Tubewells accounted for what share of India’s net irrigated area in 2021-22?
accepted.x: Tubewells accounted for 47.3 percent of the net irrigated area in 2021-22.
accepted.tq: Select the exact percentage from closely spaced alternatives and retain the reference year.
accepted.sec: Irrigation inputs - micro-irrigation, PMKSY components, PM-KUSUM, tubewell area  [APPSC, GROUP-II]
